B: Hello! Rhys, is it? I'm Rutendo.
A: Hiya, yeah. Nice to meet you.
B: I have to say, I was looking forward to this one. I saw the poster in your photo. Is it Polish?
A: It is, yeah! Erm, most people don't clock that. Sixties, I think. I collect them, sort of. And I spotted your Bauhaus one, which is a lot classier than mine.
B: Oh, it's only a print. But I love it. I'm a bit of a design nerd, you know? I did an Open University module in art history a few years ago, just for fun.
A: Just for fun, that's, yeah. I did a few online courses in colour grading and never finished them, so you're ahead of me there.
B: Ha. Colour grading, so you do film?
A: Video editing. Agency in Cardiff. Corporate stuff mostly, social ads. Erm, but I watch a lot of arthouse things, world cinema. I've got a Letterboxd I'm a bit precious about, to be honest.
B: That's funny, because I went to a Polish film night last year, at a little place in Coventry. Completely on a whim. Black and white, very long, I understood maybe half of it.
A: Oh, what was it? Do you remember?
B: Erm, I don't, I'm sorry. There was a man on a bicycle for a very long time.
A: Ha, that could be about forty films, honestly. But that's the thing, isn't it, you go to these nights and the poster's sometimes better than the film. Like, the Polish designers would get given an American western and do this mad, sort of surreal painting that had nothing to do with it. It's like they were making their own thing on the side. Sorry, I'm rambling.
B: No, I like that, making your own thing on the side. Do you do that? Make your own things?
A: Erm... a bit. Little experimental edits. I don't really show anyone.
B: Why not?
A: Dunno. They're not, erm. They're not finished, I suppose.
B: My dress has been not finished for three weeks, so I understand.
A: Lisa mentioned you sew. She was well impressed.
B: She told me about your whippet and the bins!
A: Oh no. Moss is famous now.
B: She's the star of the session. Have you had Martin yet?
A: Not yet. Erm, do you travel much, for galleries and that?
B: One proper trip a year. Lisbon, Marrakech, Copenhagen recently.
A: No way, we did Lisbon and Copenhagen. Did you go to the design museum in Copenhagen?
B: Designmuseum, yes! The chairs! A whole corridor of chairs. I spent about two hours there, I was so happy.
A: Ffion dragged me out after forty minutes. I was sort of standing in front of the posters section going, just five more minutes.
B: You need to go on your own next time. I always travel alone, then nobody drags you anywhere.
A: That's fair. I'd probably panic at the airport, though. Ffion does all the timings.
B: The airport is the worst bit. Once you're there, it's fine.
A: That's what everyone says. Erm, what do you do for work, sorry, I didn't ask.
B: Occupational therapist. Home visits, grab rails, that kind of thing. Very practical. Sometimes I wonder if I should have done something more creative, but
